The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington,
I'm Corva Coleman.
Big tech company Invidia says CEO Jensen Huang has resigned.

after he admitted an affair.

Police in Washington, D.C. say one person has died
after a mass shooting about one mile from the White House.
Other people were wounded near and in a local gym.
Police officers say a suspect barricaded himself
in a nearby apartment, but the suspect was later found
with a gunshot wound.
They believe the local threat has ended.
Last hour, Washington, D.C. Interim Police Chief,
Jeffrey Carroll, explained how the active shooting began.
>> Just before 8 o'clock this morning, a call came
in for the report of a shooting in the 1500 block,
a 15th Street inside of a gym.

They were on scene within 30 seconds.
Once they arrived on the scene, they did locate an adult male

out for additional gunshots and victims.
At this time, we have located a total of four individuals
that were shot here on the scene and transported,
and one individual who was deceased here on the scene.
>> He also said federal agencies were involved
in this response.
The incident was close to the White House.
President Trump's special envoys, Steve Whitcoff
and Jared Kushner, are in Moscow for meetings
with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
This is after U.S.-led peace talks between Russia
and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi.
NPR's Charles Maine says the U.S. wants Russia's leader
to consider European views.
>> Kushner said they want to brief Putin directly
and convince him to include Europeans in these discussions,
which are after all about European security.
>> Now, European governments are clearly nervous
about a deal being cut with Moscow over their heads,
so much so they sent envoys to Abu Dhabi to get updates
from the U.S. and Ukraine on the sidelines.
>> NPR's Charles Maine's reporting.
Israel bombed one of Gaza's biggest hospitals just
after midnight.
The hospital says the attack killed six people,
including a child and a doctor.
NPR's Aya Batrawi and Anis Baba have more.
>> Israel attacked Nasser Hospital throughout the war,
but this latest attack is the first bombardment
of the facility since a cease-fire was agreed
to last year.
The attack damaged the surgical ward and intensive care unit.
NPR's Anis Baba describes the scene.
>> When you look here, when you see inside the hospital,
it just reminds you that cease-fire is not there.
For one year now, we're talking
about 1,600 Palestinians were killed,
and today the Palestinians are being killed inside the hospital
itself, among them,
one of the most prominent surgeons in Gaza.
>> The hospital says a 13-year-old boy
and other medical staff were also killed.
Israel says it was targeting a Hamas commander
and that the hospital was used to store weapons.
Witnesses say he was wounded but survived the strike.
>> NPR's Aya Batrawi and Anis Baba, it's NPR.
New York City Mayor Zoran Mamdani says at least eight people
have been killed by the collapse
of a building yesterday in Brooklyn.
He says another 17 people have been injured,
including three firefighters.
Officials don't know how many more people
may be trapped in the rubble.
President Trump is threatening to double U.S. tariffs on Mexico.
He is pointing to news reports that hundreds of migrants
are apparently moving in Mexico toward the southern U.S. border.
Trump says he has told Mexico to stop the migrants
and that he sent warnings to Texas officials
as well as to federal immigration authorities.
A federal judge has rejected the BBC's request
to dismiss President Trump's defamation case.
The president alleges a BBC documentary
defamed him by splicing together his remarks
before the January 6th attack on the U.S. Capitol.
And Pierce David Fochenflick has more.
>> The BBC argues Trump hadn't alleged any harm.
He withdrew claims of business losses
and is seeking to avoid having to share records
of his financial holdings and dealings.
And the BBC says the 2024 documentary,
aired two weeks before the presidential elections,
wasn't shown in this country, much less Florida,
where the case was filed.
That failed to impress the presiding judge, Jeffrey Kuntz,
who was appointed by the president
and is overseeing the case.
He said the BBC's editing gave the mistaken impression
that Trump called for violence.
And the judge said the timing so close to the election
bolsters the defamation claim.
Evaluating the case's merits, Judge Kuntz wrote,
would fall to another day.
David Fochenflick, NPR News.
>> On Wall Street, the Dow is now up 150 points.
